subject: Post-demo: Lumenix dataplane pilot — cost signals & next steps
messages:

Subject: Post-demo: Lumenix dataplane pilot — cost signals & next steps

Hi Emily / Tom — thanks again for the demo time earlier. Quick recap and a few asks so we can land a clean procurement path: 

Recap (short):
- Goal: pilot Redwood inference for Lumenix dataplane feature (real-time embedding + reranking)
- Primary success metrics: 99th-pct latency < 120ms, cost per 1M tokens budget band, and production reliability during peak windows

What we need from you to put together a pricing proposal and mutual action plan: 
1) Expected monthly token volume for the pilot (best guess range). If you expect a ramp, give month 1 / month 3 / steady-state numbers.
2) Target unit economics: is there a target $/1M tokens (or a target monthly cap) you need us to hit to be viable?
3) Procurement thresholds: internal PO minimums, approval gates (e.g., does anything > $50k need procurement? > $100k need VP approval or RFP?).
4) Any legal or security gating (SOC2 evidence, IP clauses) that would affect lead time.

I've attached a short initial estimate (attachment stub: initial-estimate.xlsx) — it's intentionally conservative and shows both PAYG and small committed band examples so you have a starting point.

Next steps: if you can reply with the three items above, Marcus will craft a line-item that maps to your procurement lanes and Grace will coordinate a procurement call if needed.

Thanks — happy to hop on 30 mins next week if easier.

— Avery

From: Emily Chen <emily@lumenix.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Lumenix dataplane pilot — cost signals & next steps

Thanks Avery — great recap. Quick answers so you can build a proposal: 

1) Volume signal (pilot -> scale):
- Pilot month 1: 10M tokens/mo (spike to 18M in peak)
- Pilot month 3 (ramp): 40–60M tokens/mo
- Steady-state (post-pilot): 80–120M tokens/mo for the first 6–9 months if production goes well

2) Unit economics: our internal target for vendor unit cost is in the $180–$220 per 1M tokens range for large-scale committed pricing. For pilot we can tolerate something ~20–30% higher on PAYG, but discounts need to be visible as commitment increases.

3) Procurement thresholds and approvals:
- PO required for any vendor spend > $35,000 (procurement@lumenix.ai)
- Anything exceeding $100,000 triggers a procurement review and our sourcing team will request competitive quotes / RFP
- VP-level approval needed for multi-year commitments or any unusual IP/data clauses
- Legal lead time for standard SaaS agreement: ~4–6 weeks; if data-handling addenda needed, add 2–3 weeks

4) Security/compliance: SOC 2 Type II report required before production access. We can accept SOC 2 report plus a short attestation for on-prem options.

Attached: procurement-guidance.pdf (internal playbook) — see page 4 for PO workflow. 

Can you share a simple line-item that shows: PAYG $/1M, 3-month committed discount tiers, 6/12-month committed tiers and any per-token ceilings? That will help me route to procurement and estimate timing. We should also lock a 30-minute procurement alignment call — afternoons PST next week work for us.

Emily Chen
Head of Machine Learning Engineering | Lumenix
emily@lumenix.ai | +1 415-555-9988

Forwarding Emily's answers — key signals below and recommended approach so we can move quickly: 

Emily's signals:
- Pilot 10M -> ramp 40–60M -> steady 80–120M tokens/mo
- Target economics: $180–$220 per 1M tokens at scale; pilot can be ~20–30% higher PAYG
- PO threshold: > $35k requires procurement; > $100k triggers sourcing/RFP; legal lead time 4–6w
- SOC 2 Type II required before production

Recommended pricing stub to prepare (we should present as simple line items + a MAP):
A) PAYG: $260 / 1M tokens (no commitment) — for pilot validation
B) 3-month commitment band (min 30M total): $225 / 1M tokens
C) 6-month commitment band (min 180M total): $200 / 1M tokens
D) Annual committed/enterprise: $185 / 1M tokens (negotiable with capacity commit > 1B tokens)

Procurement play: keep the pilot under $35k where possible to avoid PO gating, or present a small initial PO + a clear ramp that shows the commit will move into the $100k+ space only after a procurement review. 

Action items:
- Marcus: prepare a line-item pricing grid and channel-specific MAP (pricing-grid.csv attached).
- Grace: line up a procurement sync and share preferred times with Emily; also check legal for SOC 2 evidence and expected redline risks.
- I will create a short MAP doc to send to Emily that maps token bands to PO thresholds and legal lead time.

— Avery

Hi Emily / Tom — thanks for the clear signals. We're aligned on how to present this to procurement. Attached is a short Mutual Action Plan (lumenix-procurement-MAP.pdf) that maps the pilot milestones to expected spend bands and the PO thresholds you called out.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Marcus will share the line-item pricing CSV by EOD tomorrow (shows PAYG / 3m / 6m / annual rows, and incremental discounts).
2) We suggest structuring the pilot as a 30–45 day validation window targeted to stay under $35k, with a staged commit option if you want to accelerate into the 40–60M ramp earlier. That keeps procurement simple and avoids a formal RFP unless you prefer otherwise.
3) Schedule a 30-minute procurement alignment call this week — afternoons PST we can do Tue/Thu. Please confirm a preferred slot.

Attachments (stubs): lumenix-procurement-MAP.pdf, pricing-grid.csv

If procurement wants a one-pager for budget owners we can produce an "expected spend" summary showing month-by-month spend at the proposed tiers (useful for PO approval). Happy to jump on the call with Marcus and Avery.

Best —
